answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a bonded registry whose stake scales with identity count. A new agent posts only a pearl-sized minimum, but shared funding, timing, or referral paths flag a cluster, so one operator running N keys pays about N times the base bond while earning one agent's reward. Honest agents recover the stake on exit, so their cost is opportunity cost, while a fraud fleet is capital the attacker must front and each extra key is a beacon for cluster analysis. A crystal-clear slashing rule then burns the bond of proven duplicates, so identity farming costs more than it earns.
